mechanism: A standardized {{solver_tree}} that orchestrates one lifecycle run for a user_request executed by a {{polymorphic_solver}}. It enforces a strict transition from Abstract to Concrete and evaluates feasibility before execution. 1. {{request_framing}} converts the request -> {{frame_spec}}. 2. {{manifest_planning}} converts the spec -> {{execution_manifest}}. Before execution, {{realizable}} judges the ExecutionManifest against the stated {{budget}}, and its Value rating must pass the declared {{criteria}}. 3. {{rollout}} executes the ExecutionManifest -> {{rollout_manifest}}. After execution, the protocol reports the resulting real-world effects as the {{outcome}}; the RolloutManifest remains the execution record rather than standing in for those effects.
gloss: Standard Interpret-Plan-Rollout workflow to ensure realizability
failure_modes: Bureaucracy: Blindly following all steps for trivial tasks.
Admission Rejection: A seam validation fails or the realizability rating does not pass {{criteria}}, and this run halts before the next phase.
Manifest-as-Outcome: The {{rollout_manifest}} is reported as the realized {{outcome}} even though it records actions rather than their real-world effects.
invariants: Typed Seams: {{request_framing}} yields {{frame_spec}}, {{manifest_planning}} yields {{execution_manifest}}, and {{rollout}} yields {{rollout_manifest}}.
Realizability Admission: Before {{rollout}}, {{realizable}} judges the {{execution_manifest}} against the stated {{budget}}, and its Value rating passes the declared {{criteria}}.
Non-Compensatory: A failed seam validation or realizability criterion halts this run; iteration requires a new run or an enclosing loop.
postconditions: On successful completion, {{outcome}} is reported separately from the frozen {{rollout_manifest}}.
On a rejected seam or failed realizability criterion, this run halts before the next phase.
